title: Unify traffic-splitting workflows for model rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: We currently have fragmented traffic-splitting semantics across Hosted (control-plane driven), Dedicated (reserved pools with autoscale proxies), and Private (customer-managed control plane or air-gapped). This leads to inconsistent canary behavior, manual A/B wiring, and ad-hoc shadowing for customers on Private deployments. Goal: Provide a single declarative workflow and runtime primitives that enable canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadow traffic, and deterministic auto-rollback with the same semantics across all deployment modes, while respecting environment-specific constraints (networking, control-plane availability, KMS/HSM policies, RBAC).
acceptance_criteria: A declarative 'traffic-split' API (JSON/YAML) that supports weighted traffic, match rules, and shadow routes is documented and available in Redwood API/console
Hosted mode implements server-side traffic splitting with progressive weights and automatic metrics checks for auto-rollback
Dedicated mode provides a compatible control surface that translates splits to pool routing rules and can be controlled via the existing routing service

Private mode supports a self-contained operator (k8s/operator or binary) that applies the same high-level config locally; when control-plane is not reachable, shall operate with local policy and emit telemetry to customer-provided endpoints
A/B experiments are expressible via named routes and provide rollout analytics in Console within the release window
Shadow traffic can be toggled per-route with percentage and does not affect SLO for primary route; resource quotas prevent overload
Auto-rollback triggers (latency/error/regression thresholds) are configurable and validated in a dry-run mode prior to release
E2E test harness (integration + simulated network partitions) validates parity for canary weight progression and rollback behavior across at least one Hosted, one Dedicated, and one Private cluster
Security review completed and audit logs include route changes, who initiated rollout, and auto-rollback events
tasks: Design: finalize traffic-split API schema and mappings for runtime (owner: Diego)
Infra: extend routing service to accept weighted rules and shadow annotations (owner: Priya Shah)
Dedicated: implement pool translation layer for reserved capacity (owner: Marco Li)
Private: build operator shim that consumes traffic-split config and applies local routing (owner: Yvonne Chen)
Console: UI for canary configuration, real-time weight controls, and rollback buttons (owner: Rahul Gupta)
Telemetry: add rollout events and auto-rollback signals to event pipeline and Console dashboards (owner: Lin Zhao)
E2E tests: create test cases including network partition and KMS unavailability scenarios (owner: SRE team)
Docs & Examples: Confluence runbook + three example manifests (hosted/dedicated/private) (owner: Docs)
Security: threat model review and KMS/HSM handling in Private mode (owner: Security)
Launch: coordinate with Solutions and Customer Success for early access customers
design_decisions: Single declarative API: use an environment-agnostic schema (traffic-split.v1) that maps to runtime-specific adapters
Progressive rollout controller: controller moves weights in steps based on metric checks; controller runs in control-plane for Hosted, in management plane for Dedicated, and as operator for Private
Shadowing implementation: use copy-without-affect semantics — mirror request to candidate model instance but discard replica responses unless debugging is enabled
Auto-rollback policy: support both absolute thresholds and relative regression compared to baseline; default 3 evaluation windows with 95th percentile latency and error-rate checks
Fail-safe: if control-plane is unreachable, Private operator will keep last-known config and expose a read-only view; manual overrides require local RBAC
constraints: Private deployments may be air-gapped: no assumption of outbound telemetry; must support pushing metrics to customer endpoints
Dedicated pools have resource reservation semantics: cannot exceed pool quotas when increasing canary weight without autoscale policy
Hosted mode must preserve multi-tenant isolation and per-tenant rate limits while performing traffic splits
KMS/HSM policies in Private can require customer-managed key rotation; rollout controller cannot store plaintext keys
Network egress costs and cross-AZ latency must be considered when shadowing high-volume routes
rollout_matrix: Hosted: control-plane orchestrates weight progression; metrics computed centrally; auto-rollback can trigger global rollback or per-tenant rollback; Console provides one-click abort

Dedicated: management-plane issues pool-level routing updates; supports canary within a pool or across pools; controller must coordinate with autoscaler to reserve burst capacity before increasing canary weight

Private (connected): operator polls central config; can be run in 'controller' or 'agent-only' modes depending on customer preference; operator performs local metric checks and can trigger local rollback
Private (air-gapped): offline manifest apply; customer runs operator to enact splits manually; diagnostic mode required for preflight validation; CI/CD hooks recommended for controlled rollouts
testing_plan: Unit tests for traffic-split schema validation and adapter mappings
Integration tests that simulate stepwise weight increases and validate rollback for latency and error thresholds
Shadowing load test: ensure primary SLOs unaffected at 2x incoming QPS for mirrored requests
E2E against a Dedicated staging cluster with reserved pools to validate quota enforcement
Private operator acceptance tests including KMS failure, control-plane disconnect, and manual rollback flows
Chaos tests: network partition between control-plane and operator to ensure safe fallback
Regression tests for telemetry and audit log generation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow traffic can double resource usage and impact cost — Mitigation: enforce default cap and require explicit opt-in for high-volume routes
Risk: Private air-gapped installs may drift from Hosted semantics — Mitigation: operator includes a compatibility checker and preflight dry-run
Risk: Auto-rollback may flip-flop on noisy signals — Mitigation: add configurable stabilization windows, require multiple failing windows to trigger rollback
Risk: Dedicated pools may not have spare capacity to ramp canary — Mitigation: integrate with autoscaler for temporary reserved burst or fail early with clear error
Risk: Security concerns when transporting rollout policies — Mitigation: encrypt manifests in transit, use KMS/HSM, and record all changes in audit logs
